item.title: East Mississippi set to open softball season with five scheduled home doubleheaders in February
item.description: With five scheduled home doubleheaders during the month of February, East Mississippi Community College’s 2026 softball season is slated to get started with a home twin bill against Marion Military Institute Tuesday on the Scooba campus.

item.title: City moves forward with Jaycee parking, other projects
item.description: The Meridian City Council voted Tuesday to move forward with several ongoing projects throughout the city after hearing from city officials about the work.

item.title: Deadline extended to Feb. 6 for sophomores to apply for State Board of Education 2026-27 junior rep spot
item.description: Due to inclement weather that impacted much of Mississippi, the application deadline for the Mississippi State Board of Education Junior Student Representative position has been extended to Feb. 6.

item.title: Late run lifts Newton County over Northeast Lauderdale

item.title: Central United Methodist to host Mardi Gras Mission Meal
item.description: Central United Methodist Church invites the community to a celebration of Fat (Shrove) Tuesday, Feb. 17, with a traditional Mardi Gras Meal of shrimp and crab gumbo, rice, French bread, and very special bread pudding.

item.title: Marion aldermen hire lobbying firm to represent town at State Capitol
item.description: The town of Marion will have a larger presence at the State Capitol this year after the Board of Aldermen voted Tuesday to hire a lobbying firm to represent the town’s interests.

item.title: Wicker: proposed ICE facility threatens Byhalia economy and infrastructure
item.description: U.S. Sen. Roger Wicker sent a letter to the Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem on Tuesday expressing opposition to a proposed plan to convert a warehouse in Byhalia into an Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention center.

item.title: Meridian Mardi Gras kicks off Saturday at 11 a.m.
item.description: The streets of Meridian will be decorated with purple, green and gold Saturday as the Arts and Community Events Society hosts its annual Meridian Mardi Gras celebration at City Hall lawn.
